explanation:
[EFFECT] The hour of day has a strongly non-monotonic, double-peaked effect on predicted bike demand. Contributions are deeply negative in the early morning hours, hitting their lowest point around 4–5 a.m. (roughly −3.5 in log space, meaning the model multiplies its baseline demand estimate way down for that hour). Demand contributions rise sharply through the morning, reaching a modest positive peak around 8–9 a.m., then level off through mid-day before climbing again to the highest positive peak around 5 p.m. (hour 17, ~+1.0 in log space). After the evening peak, contributions steadily fall again through the late night hours.

[IMPORTANCE] Hour of day is by far the single most important feature in the model, ranked 1st with an importance score of 0.83 — more than four times larger than the next-most-important features (year and temperature, both around 0.20). Knowing the hour alone drives more of the demand prediction than any other factor.

[RECOMMENDATION] Since the 5 p.m. hour drives the highest predicted demand and the pre-dawn hours drive it to near zero, bike availability and staff deployment should be concentrated in the afternoon–evening commute window (especially 4–7 p.m.) and can be scaled back significantly during the overnight hours (midnight–5 a.m.) to optimise resources.
